source: Maniscalco M, Weitzberg E, Sundberg J et al. Eur Respir J 2003;22:323-329, doi:10.1183/09031936.03.00017903 (model part). Same model and text in US Patent 7,270,638 B2.
verified: 2026-11-21 against the full text at publications.ersnet.org/content/erj/22/2/323 and patents.google.com/patent/US7270638B2 (previous version of this file was transcribed via a summarising fetch).
setup: Syringe (= sinus) filled with NO 2-10 ppm, connected horizontally via a Luer fitting to a plastic cylinder (= nasal cavity); the syringe tip is the ostium. Tip diameter varied 0.8-4.0 mm. Tip LENGTH and how the diameters were made are NOT REPORTED in either the paper or the patent. Cylinder distal end open (~1 cmH2O) or via a 50 cmH2O/L/s resistor (~10 cmH2O). NO output = flow x concentration at the distal end (nL/min).

standard_setting.note: human standard is 150 Hz by inference: the human standard output 175±8 nL/min equals the 150 Hz value. The authors calculated the standard system's resonance as 200 Hz (Durrant & Lovrinic formula; tip length not given).

fig6_exchange_percent.what: fraction of syringe NO gone after ONE 10-s human hum (0.2 L/s), from syringe NO before/after; read from Fig. 6 (patent Fig. 7), +-2 points

no_output_ratio_vs_smallest.note: ratios as printed. They disagree with Fig. 6 (exchange ratio 1:8:12.5:13.5:16) and cannot all be at the standard setting: 30 x (1/6) x 175 nL/min over 10 s exceeds the 120 nL of NO in the syringe.

absolute_output_nL_per_min.note: (175-27.7)/6 = 25 nL in 10 s = ~20% of the 120 nL in the syringe, whereas Fig. 6 gives 75% at 1.9 mm. Internal inconsistency of ~3.5x between the two ways of measuring exchange.

frequency_response_nL_per_min.note: the artificial frequencies come from three different duck calls, so the sound amplitude changes with frequency too

table1_resonance_vs_hum_nL_per_min.note: conditions not stated; values far above the standard 295, so not the standard setting

volume_note: clerical errors, checked 2026-11-21: the text's ratios are swapped between the two models (artificial table = 1:2.0:3.7:5.4, matching the ratio the text gives for HUMAN), and the human 5 mL entry (79±1.0) is copied from the artificial table; with 5 mL = 35 the human table gives 1:2.5:5.0:7.0, the ratio the text gives for ARTIFICIAL.

pressure_1_to_10_cmH2O.note: 175±8 is the human standard value and 250±3.4 carries the artificial standard's sem (295±3.4), so the labels look swapped again; the human model then rises with pressure, as in vivo (807 -> 932 nL/min).

concentration_note: human 10 ppm = 416 nL/min is 7.3x the 2 ppm value for a 5x concentration; output should scale with concentration, so this entry is suspect. The artificial series is linear (1:2.1:3.9:5.7).
reliability: Qualitative trends agree across both measures and both models (humming >> silent; strong ostium-size dependence with a steep step between 0.8 and 1.3 mm and saturation near 4 mm; frequency matters). Individual numbers: single bench study, repeat SEMs only, several clerical errors in the model section. Use for shape, not for fits tighter than about 10 points or a factor of ~1.5.
